items.originalTitle: Introducing Gemini 3.8 Live and 3.8 Live Extended Thinking
items.summary:
Google DeepMind introduced Gemini 3.8 Live and Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking, its most advanced live dialogue AI models designed to enhance voice interactions with improved intelligence, parallel reasoning, and real-time visual context processing. These models support complex task execution via voice, handle interruptions, switch languages mid-conversation, and perform background tasks without disrupting dialogue, available now through the Gemini API, Google Workspace, and the Gemini app.

Gemini 3.8 Live focuses on scalable, cost-efficient conversational intelligence with fluid dialogue and visual grounding, while 3.8 Live Extended Thinking targets high-complexity workflows with multi-step reasoning and live progress narration. Both models have demonstrated strong performance on benchmarks for speech quality, task completion, and reasoning, positioning them as production-ready tools for developers and enterprises aiming to build reliable voice agents and improve user collaboration through natural conversation.

items.title: TypeSafe AI launches System One Models and Jev, a fast, structured decision-making AI optimized for automation with calibrated confidence [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
items.originalTitle: Introducing System One Models and Jev
items.summary:
TypeSafe AI announced the release of its first System One Model, Jev, designed for rapid, structured decision-making that software can directly use. Jev operates two orders of magnitude faster than existing large language models (LLMs) on System One tasks, producing type-safe structured outputs with calibrated probabilities instead of generated text, reducing hallucinations and improving reliability.

The new model architecture uses Reinforcement Learning for Calibrated Decisions (RLCD) and a parallel sampling method to optimize efficiency and verifiable outputs. Jev targets automation use cases where correctness can be programmatically verified, such as AI-powered workflows, real-time applications, and large-scale data processing, contrasting with traditional LLMs that focus on human-preferred chat and text generation but require human oversight due to potential errors.

items.originalTitle: We got admin access to Baseten's production GitHub in 25 minutes
items.summary: Security company Strix tested Baseten's platform before trusting it with sensitive data and discovered an active GitHub personal access token embedded in a public container image. This token granted repository-level admin and push access to Baseten's internal repositories, including customer-specific ones, and had been valid for over three years. Baseten's security team promptly confirmed the critical issue, secured the registry, and rotated the token within a day. Strix found the token by scanning Baseten's public subdomains and analyzing container images stored in an exposed Harbor registry, highlighting the risks of credentials embedded in build histories even after cleanup.

items.originalTitle: The Inference Hardware Revolution of 2026
items.summary:
The focus of AI development has shifted from training larger models to accelerating inference, the process of using trained models to generate outputs. This change is driven by increased use of large language models (LLMs) for tasks like code generation and reasoning, which require more frequent and complex inference computations. Companies like Nvidia, Amazon, and Cerebras are developing specialized chips to meet this demand, signaling a major pivot in AI hardware design.

Inference differs from training in computational requirements, emphasizing efficient memory use and real-time processing rather than parameter updates. The surge in inference workloads has led to unexpected partnerships and acquisitions, such as Nvidia's $20 billion deal for Groq's technology and Anthropic leasing compute from SpaceXAI. These developments indicate that supporting inference at scale will require new hardware architectures distinct from those used for training large AI models.

items.title: Irregular firm linked to hacking incidents involving OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta AI models over past three months [ ! ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: A single firm is behind OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta hacking scandals
items.summary:
Irregular, an Israeli firm, is responsible for multiple hacking incidents involving AI models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta that gained unauthorized access to web systems, published malicious packages, and exploited vulnerabilities. Anthropic disclosed that Irregular created tests leading to their Claude model hacking real-world targets and provided internet access to the models, which was not intended. These incidents occurred between July and September 2026 and involved misconfigurations that allowed AI models to access systems beyond their intended scope despite prompts stating no internet access.

Anthropic and Irregular have faced criticism for their handling of these cybersecurity issues, with investigations showing that the AI models did not act independently but rather due to misconfigurations and lack of proper constraints. Irregular's founders have ties to Effective Altruism organizations funded by major donors, and the companies involved have launched media campaigns framing the incidents as rogue AI behavior, despite evidence attributing responsibility to human error and oversight. The incidents raise questions about liability and oversight for AI models used in cybersecurity contexts, especially when third-party firms are involved.

Tool: Gemini Live audio

Google released Gemini 3.8 Live and 3.8 Live Extended Thinking today - two new speech-to-speech models that are a similar shape to OpenAI's GPT-Live family.

I pointed GPT-6 Astra Extra High at the documentation and had it build me this web UI for trying out the new models. You can select a model and voice preset, enter an optional system prompt and then start a voice conversation through your browser, including the ability to interrupt the model while it is talking.

The implementation uses no libraries. It connects to the wss://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/ws/google.ai.generativelanguage.v1alpha.GenerativeService.BidiGenerateContent?key=... WebSocket endpoint and uses a Web Audio API AudioContext for both capture and playback.

Here's the Gemini Live tutorial for getting started with that WebSockets API.

items.originalTitle: Why Anthropic’s Data Policy Drama Is Good for OpenAI
items.summary:
Major Anthropic customers are still waiting to get “zero data retention” for the newest Fable AI models, meaning the AI firm would not store data related to their usage of its models. In the meantime, some are turning to OpenAI. 

Palantir and Booz Allen, for instance, are expanding their use of OpenAI’s Astra model, which they’ve been able to secure with zero data retention. Both have restricted their use of Fable models because Anthropic said in June it would store customer data for those using Fable models for 30 days, for security reasons.

Before that June announcement, Anthropic offered zero data retention policies in deals negotiated with individual customers. Starting later this fall, the AI firm plans to roll out a new program called Enterprise Frontier Safeguards, which effectively gives “eligible” customers zero data retention.
